Finally, we evaluate fractional-Chern-insulator stability criteria analytically and quantify the lowest band of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model to be a nearly ideal Chern band. Our approach opens a route for studying also the quantum geometry of other sublattice-symmetric multiband systems.

papers.title_en: Exact dynamics of spinning particles and the spin wall in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.abstract_en: The motion of a spinning test body is governed by the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon equations and deviates from geodesics already at first order in the spin. Most studies of this problem truncate the dynamics at linear order; here we solve the equatorial, spin-aligned problem in Schwarzschild spacetime at all orders in the spin under the Tulczyjew--Dixon condition. Eliminating the four-velocity casts the system into a closed algebraic form and reduces the motion to a single first-order radial equation. Keeping track of both kinematical masses, the norm of the four-momentum and its projection on the velocity, we find that the representative worldline ceases to be timelike on a surface in the space of radius, spin and angular momentum. We call this surface the spin wall. It bounds the radii accessible to a spinning body and is present for every nonvanishing value of the momentum's angular component; only for the purely radial family does it collapse, and that family moves on a geodesic. Its position follows in closed form and may lie inside the horizon, enclose it, or reach the exterior, the last possibility arising already at small spin. We also examine how far the pole--dipole truncation remains under control where the wall is accessible. Within that regime we determine the circular orbits and their stability, the spin dependence of the marginally stable orbit, and the perihelion advance beyond first order in the spin.

papers.title_en: Analogue Schwinger Pair Production in Acoustic Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: We show that an analogue Schwinger pair production can be realized in Reissner-Nordstr{ö}m-like acoustic black holes constructed from a Bose-Einstein condensate subject to a synthetic vector potential. Upon Kaluza-Klein reduction of the five-dimensional acoustic geometry, the higher-dimensional phonon modes appear as effectively charged phonons in the resulting four-dimensional spacetime, in which the electric field experienced by the charged phonons arises from the component of the synthetic vector potential along the compactified direction. Then by appropriately choosing the background flow velocity and the synthetic vector potential, the reduced acoustic metric can take the form of a Reissner-Nordstr{ö}m-like black hole. From this metric we obtain the mean number of spontaneously produced phonon pairs in both the extremal and near extremal cases, and show that in the extremal limit this mean number takes the form of the Schwinger formula. Moreover, charged-phonon pair production not only admits the same effective thermal interpretation as Schwinger pair production of real charged particles, but can also be interpreted as the analogue Hawking radiation and superradiance from the five-dimensional perspective. Finally, we make estimates of pair production using experimental parameters in Bose-Einstein condensate, providing theoretical guidance for future laboratory detection.

papers.title_en: The Weyl Tensor for Gravitational-Wave Causal Sets: Thickness of Geodesic Analogs and Geodesic Deviation
papers.abstract_en: Causal set theory proposes that spacetime is replaced by a partially ordered set (a directed acyclic graph) at the smallest scales. This graph is postulated to produce all the features of continuous geometry above some discreteness scale. We develop an approach to sprinkling causal sets into a linearized plane gravitational wave spacetime, and report on the feasibility of using the analog of geodesic deviation to find a component of the Weyl tensor for such causal sets. We take the collection of all longest chains between a pair of elements to be the discrete analog of the timelike geodesic between them and find through numerical simulations in Minkowski spacetime of various dimensions that the spread or "thickness" of the collection increases with chain length. We estimate, assuming an ideal element-to-element spatial distance estimator and a wave of amplitude $h_0 = 10^{-2}$, that at least $N_{\mathrm{total}} \gtrsim \mathcal{O}(10^8)$ elements are needed to overcome the noise introduced by the thickness and detect the curvature. This is beyond the $\mathcal{O}(10^6)$ elements we can currently simulate. Future work may show ways of extracting more information from the sprinkled causal set and hence lowering the estimate for $N_{\mathrm{total}}$.

papers.title_en: An information-theoretic framework for quantifying coherence in the cosmic density field
papers.abstract_en: We introduce an information-theoretic framework for quantifying the coherence retained in the cosmic density field across cosmic time. Using mutual information between density fields at different redshifts in cosmological $N$-body simulations, and subtracting an appropriate reference baseline, we isolate the excess statistical dependence generated by gravitational evolution. Unlike conventional clustering statistics, this approach is sensitive to nonlinear and higher-order correlations and directly measures the shared information between different cosmic epochs. The shared mutual information exhibits a strong dependence on spatial scale, increasing as the density field is progressively coarse-grained, reaching a maximum, and declining at larger scales. Through a series of tests involving different simulation volumes, discretization schemes, alternative baseline constructions, and subvolume analyses, we show that the location of this maximum is governed primarily by finite-sampling effects in the mutual information estimator rather than by a fundamental physical coherence scale. The observed peak therefore provides an empirical indication of the range over which the present estimator yields robust measurements. We further demonstrate that the mutual information is sensitive to cosmic evolution and cosmological parameters. Our analysis shows that filamentary environments retain more statistically accessible shared information between cosmic epochs than sheets and clusters. We also note that the shared information between the initial and present-day density fields is found to be positive but extremely small, reflecting the progressive redistribution of information during nonlinear structure formation. Our results establish mutual information as a powerful new tool for quantifying coherence, memory, and information retention in the large-scale structure of the Universe.

papers.title_en: Dynamical formation of Gaia neutron star binaries in star clusters as a phase-dependent process
papers.abstract_en: Gaia has discovered dormant compact-object binaries in which the compact object shows no observable interaction with its luminous companion. These systems, hereafter Gaia BHs and Gaia NSs for black hole (BH) and neutron star (NS) companions, provide a new probe of compact-object binary formation. These detached systems are difficult to produce through standard isolated binary evolution alone, and their formation pathways remain unclear. Previous $N$-body studies have shown that Gaia BH-like objects are formed efficiently in star clusters, while Gaia NS-like objects are not. This has been attributed to the BH subsystem dominating the cluster core. We performed direct $N$-body simulations of $10^4 \mathrm{M}_\odot$ star clusters in a Galactic tidal field and investigated how NS-main-sequence (NS-MS) binaries form during the late BH-depleted phase. We found that NS-MS binaries satisfying Gaia-sensitive criteria form only after BH depletion. NSs are present in the core throughout the evolution, but the strong encounters there are monopolized by the BH subsystem until it is depleted. Our results show that the dynamical formation of Gaia-sensitive NS-MS systems is not prevented in star clusters, but delayed relative to Gaia BH-like systems.

papers.title_en: Probing flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions with the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos
papers.abstract_en: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos probe non-standard neutrino interactions over cosmological distances. We study flavor-dependent interactions between neutrinos and dark matter (DM) for neutrinos produced inside the dense DM spike surrounding the supermassive black hole of the blazar TXS~0506+056. A flavor-diagonal potential $V_α=A_α\,ρ_χ(r)$ induced by coherent forward scattering modifies the mixing in the medium, and the flavor-dependent scattering cross section attenuates the neutrino flux along the line of sight. We show that the propagation is adiabatic throughout the spike and the halo, so that the matter eigenstates produced at the source are conserved and only re-projected onto flavors at Earth. Two regimes emerge. For $A\ll 10^{-38}\,{\rm cm^3}$ the mixing is unaffected and the IceCube three-flavor composition limits the cross section to $σ_{νχ}/m_χ\lesssim 10^{-28}\,{\rm cm^2/GeV}$. For larger $A$ the interacting flavor is isolated into a single matter eigenstate at the source; the two remaining eigenstates escape without attenuation, producing a survival plateau that relaxes the limits by up to four orders of magnitude. The sign of the potential can differ between neutrinos and antineutrinos, so that the isolated state connects to different vacuum mass eigenstates for $ν$ and $\barν$, which leaves a characteristic imprint on the flavor composition even without attenuation. The requirement that the potential induced by the dark matter density around Earth do not affect the observed PMNS matrix, so that the flavor projection at Earth is performed with the local matter mixing, gives A$\lesssim 10^{-30}\text{cm} ^3$. The combined constraints are presented in the $(A,σ_{νχ}/m_χ)$ plane and compared with a vector-mediator benchmark.

papers.title_en: Baryon Number Susceptibilities of Hot and Dense Nuclear Matter in Relativistic Mean-Field Models
papers.abstract_en: We develop a fully analytical framework for calculating baryon number susceptibilities in relativistic mean-field (RMF) models of hot and dense nuclear matter at finite temperature and baryon chemical potential. The formalism is applied to representative nonlinear RMF parameterization sets to investigate the model dependence of baryon number fluctuations over a wide range of temperatures and baryon chemical potentials. All the considered RMF parameterizations reproduce the overall qualitative beam-energy dependence of the cumulant ratios. The observed skewness and kurtosis within the RMF models satisfy the experimental values. Specifically, the FSU-family parameterizations exhibit relatively small deviations from the measured heavy-ion observables i.e. cumulant ratios.

papers.title_en: Induction instead of Feynman diagrams, L-functionals instead of Hilbert space
papers.abstract_en: The main result of this paper is a construction of an inductive process that can replace Feynman diagrams. Combining this result with the notion of the L-functional, one can give an exposition of QED that does not suffer from infrared divergences

papers.title_en: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
papers.abstract_en: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time. We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian $SU(2)$ symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes $U(1)$ and $Z_2$ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.

papers.title_en: Framing Anomaly in Lattice Chern-Simons-Maxwell Theory
papers.abstract_en: Framing anomaly is a key property of $(2+1)d$ chiral topological orders, for it reveals that the chirality is an intrinsic bulk property of the system, rather than a property of the boundary between two systems. Understanding framing anomaly in lattice models is particularly interesting, as concrete, solvable lattice models of chiral topological orders are rare. In a previous work, we defined and solved the $U(1)$ Chern-Simons-Maxwell theory on spacetime lattice, showing its chiral edge mode and the associated gravitational anomaly on boundary. In this work, we show its framing anomaly in the absence of boundary, by computing the expectation of a lattice version of the modular $T$ operator in the ground subspace on a spatial torus, from which we extract that $\langle T \rangle$ has a universal phase of $-2π/12$ as expected: $-2π/8$ from the Gauss-Milgram sum of the topological spins of the ground states, and $2π/24$ from the framing anomaly; we can also extract the $2π/24$ framing anomaly phase alone from the full spectrum of $T$ in the ground subspace by computing $\langle T^m \rangle$. This pins down the last and most crucial property required for a valid lattice definition of $U(1)$ Chern-Simons theory.

papers.title_en: Rotation slows the instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
papers.abstract_en: Rotation weakens the radial instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in slow-rotation perturbation theory. We investigate its nonlinear effect by evolving stationary rotating drainholes supported by a phantom scalar field. We construct the backgrounds with an independent spectral solver, validate them against published symmetric solutions, and identify a misprint in a published field equation that did not affect the original authors' numerical results. Evolutions perturbed only by discretization error show that rotation slows the collapse. At intermediate spins some throats expand, with the direction of departure depending on the effective perturbation. At the fastest evolved spin, the throat's areal radius shows no growing departure through evolution time $t=150$ in code units, about 28 e-folding times of the static instability, at three resolutions. Two other rapidly rotating models also show no growth over their reliable evolution intervals. Collapsing rotating throats emit an axisymmetric quadrupolar gravitational-wave burst whose energy increases between the two spins compared. Second-order initial data excite the instability through their background truncation error. The results establish slower collapse and prolonged absence of detected radial growth for the sampled asymmetric backgrounds, over finite times from initially axisymmetric data.

papers.title_en: Relativistic mode sums for neutron-star tidal response
papers.abstract_en: Time-dependent tidal interactions during the late inspiral of binary neutron stars encode valuable information about neutron-star structure, but systematically extending the familiar Newtonian mode-sum picture into full general relativity is nontrivial. In this paper, we develop a practical relativistic implementation of mode-sum tidal response for non-rotating neutron stars in Regge-Wheeler gauge. Using near-zone boundary conditions, we systematically define the interior tidal field, the relativistic overlap integrals, and the corresponding mode amplitudes. The good is that the dominant f-mode contribution is remarkably robust, reproducing the direct matching calculation to within $\sim 3$\% across the equations of state we consider. The bad is that the operator governing mode inner product is not positive definite on the full Regge-Wheeler-gauge function space, so the relativistic mode sum truncated at ${\cal{O}}(ω^2)$ is not expected to strictly converge to the direct matching solution. The subtle is that the tidal field inside the star is not unique, although this ambiguity has only a limited impact on the dominant f-mode response for the classes of extensions studied here. Our results establish the practical utility of relativistic mode-sum approximations, while making clear that their predictive power comes from a controlled low-mode description, rather than from a formally convergent strong-field expansion.

papers.title_en: Effects of Solar Wind Plasma Noise on Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background Searches with a Space Based Interferometer Network
papers.abstract_en: The LISA-Taiji dual detector network improves millihertz SGWB sensitivity through cross correlation measurements. Solar wind plasma, however, can generate plasma noise correlated between detectors and bias SGWB cross correlation estimates. We use high time resolution electron density data from Wind/SWE, estimate the solar wind electron density fluctuation spectrum with the Lomb-Scargle method, and propagate the resulting plasma noise to the TDI A/E channels of the LISA-Taiji network. By including finite arm propagation, Taylor frozen flow spatial correlations, and the network overlap reduction response, we compute the SGWB parameter bias induced by interdetector plasma noise. Although the single detector plasma residual is below the reference noise, the component correlated between detectors can enter the SGWB cross correlation estimator directly. Under dual detector scale coverage, the plasma induced parameter bias for a power law SGWB can reach $12.73\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty. For M2/M3 cosmic string spectra, the bias in $\ln Gμ$ can reach $19.26\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty for the network configurations, observing times, and frequency bands considered here. These results show that the impact of solar wind plasma noise cannot be assessed from the single detector residual noise level alone. In LISA-Taiji SGWB searches, the interdetector correlated component of this noise can directly affect parameter estimation.

papers.title_en: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
papers.abstract_en: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalize the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including a general axial condition that allows for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behavior of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.

papers.title_en: Weak-field analytical solutions for f(R,L_matt) gravity in a static and spherically symmetric space-time for perfect fluids
papers.abstract_en: We study the weak-field regime of $f(R,\lmatt)$ gravity for a static and spherically symmetric configuration described by a perfect fluid, whose energy density is perturbed about a constant reference value. By means of a weak-field limit expansion about a Minkowski geometric background and under a quasi-Newtonian approximation, we derive and analytically solve the coupled system that governs the gravitational perturbations and the matter variables. The solution contains the long-range Newtonian contribution and Yukawa-type corrections in the temporal and radial components of the metric. In the matter sector, the energy density, the internal energy, and the pressure acquire radial contributions, with a non-zero constant background rest-mass energy density and vanishing background internal energy and pressure. The results show how the non-minimal coupling between curvature and matter jointly modifies the geometry and the fluid in the considered regime.

papers.title_en: Equatorial Periodic Orbits and Gravitational Wave Signatures in Weyl Geometric Gravity Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: Weyl geometric gravity theory is a gravitational theory with Lagrangian density constructed from the square of the Weyl curvature scalar and the strength of the Weyl vector. The theory can be reformulated as a scalar - vector - tensor theory in the Riemann geometry by introducing an auxiliary scalar field, in the presence of a non - minimal coupling between the Ricci scalar and the scalar field. Assuming that the Weyl vector has only a radial component, an exact spherically symmetric black hole type solution of the field equations in the vacuum can be obtained. The solution depends on three arbitrary integration constants. As compared to the case of the Schwarzschild black hole, the Weyl geometric gravity black hole solution contains two new terms, linear and quadratic, in the radial coordinate. It is the main goal of the present work to investigate astrophysical properties of the Weyl geometric black holes by considering the behavior of the timelike geodesics, which allows to explore how the geometric nonmetricity influences the strong-field dynamics of massive test particles as well as the topological structure of the periodic orbits. The resulting gravitational wave emission in extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) systems is also considered. Our results show that the presence of nonmetricity in Weyl geometric gravity leaves distinct and measurable signatures on both the orbital topology and the emitted gravitational waveforms of compact EMRI systems. These unique temporal and amplitude modulations provide a promising observational avenue for testing the presence of nonmetricity on cosmic scales.

papers.title_en: 3D Hydrodynamic Simulations of Micro-Tidal Disruption Events Favor a Narrow, Ultra-relativistic Jet for GRB250702B
papers.abstract_en: The longest detected $γ$-ray burst, GRB250702B, exhibited seven hours of prompt $γ$-ray emission, a day-long X-ray precursor, and a weeks-long fading X-ray tail. We show that a jetted micro-TDE can explain this unusual evolution by satisfying tight constraints imposed on the engine by the requirements of jet stability and observed energetics. Using 3D hydrodynamic AREPO simulations of a $1M_\odot$ star disrupted by a $10M_\odot$ black hole, we find that within several hours the debris forms a quasi-steady envelope, with a low-density polar funnel ($ρ\propto r^{-2}$; half-opening angle $\approx15^\circ$). Applying an analytic jet stability model to the simulated envelope, we find that luminous ULGRBs operate their jets near the stability threshold. Thus, many ULGRB jets are too weak to break out and perish inside their envelopes, implying the existence of a class of low-luminosity ULGRBs powered by failed jets. Powerful ($L_{\rm jet}\gtrsim{\rm few}\times10^{47}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$), ultra-relativistic ($γ_{\rm j}\sim100$), narrowly collimated ($θ_{\rm b}\simeq 1^\circ$) jets can survive the current-driven kink instability, escape, and reproduce the observed high isotropic-equivalent luminosity of $\sim10^{51}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$. After breakout, jet widening ($θ_{\rm b}\propto t$), combined with wind-suppressed accretion ($L_{\rm jet}\propto t^{-2}$), produces the steep early X-ray decline ($L_{\rm X,iso}\propto t^{-4}$); once the jet widens to the scale of the funnel walls, its opening angle saturates at $\simeq 10^\circ$, and the decline returns to the intrinsic $t^{-2}$. Together, our simulations and jet stability constraints favor narrow, highly relativistic jets as the engines of luminous ULGRBs and predict early jet breaks, motivating early multi-wavelength follow-up of future events.

papers.title_en: Kinetic magnetohydrodynamics and Landau fluid closure in relativity
papers.abstract_en: Diffuse accretion flows near a supermassive black hole are fundamentally weakly collisional. In such weakly collisional plasmas, the ion and electron distribution functions can deviate significantly from thermal equilibrium, and particle kinetic effects can influence large-scale fluid motion by driving pressure anisotropy, heat conduction, and plasma instabilities. Modeling these plasma effects in highly relativistic flows could be important for interpreting horizon-scale observations of black hole images. In this paper, we present a theoretical framework for understanding weakly collisional plasmas in general relativity by deriving the relativistic drift kinetic equations from the Vlasov-Maxwell equations. We present the evolution equations for the moments of the gyroaveraged distribution function and introduce a new analytic Landau fluid closure to capture anisotropic heat flow in relativistic plasmas. Unlike standard (collisional) general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics or extended magnetohydrodynamics, our model does not rely on strong collisions to enforce thermal equilibrium and consistently incorporates Landau damping in a fluid closure. The model introduced in this work provides a complementary approach to fully kinetic simulations in understanding weakly collisional effects in low-luminosity relativistic black hole accretion disks.

papers.title_en: Isospectrality breaking in the axial quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordström black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity
papers.abstract_en: We study odd-parity perturbations of Reissner-Nordström black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity. The dCS action is parity invariant because $\vartheta\,{}^{*}RR$ is the product of two pseudoscalars; nevertheless, the pseudoscalar perturbation has odd parity and enters only the axial sector at linear order and so lifts the axial--polar isospectrality of general relativity. We derive the finite-charge couplings between the pseudoscalar and the axial gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations directly from the linearized field equations. Both directions are governed by the radial kernel $(Mr-Q^2)Δ/r^8$, and at nonzero charge the pseudoscalar couples to $Ψ+χΨ_e$, with $χ=2Q/[r\sqrt{(l-1)(l+2)}]$. After diagonalizing the Einstein--Maxwell sector, we compute branch-resolved quasinormal-mode shifts with exterior complex scaling for the photon-sphere modes and Frobenius shooting for the near-extremal zero-damping modes. For the Schwarzschild $l=2$ fundamental mode we obtain $β\,δω=-0.7733-0.3946\,i$ (units $M=α=1$). Off resonance, the gravitational-led shift scales as $ζ\,l^3$ at $Q=0$ but as $ζ\,l^2/Q$ at fixed nonzero charge and large $l$. The electromagnetic-led branch becomes exactly degenerate with the pseudoscalar mode at $Q_c=2M\sqrt{l(l+1)+1}/[l(l+1)+2]$, where the pseudoscalar potential coincides with the polar partner of the electromagnetic-led potential; there the breaking is $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtζ)$, $M|Δω|\simeq2.4\sqrtζ$ for $l=2$, and the shift reverses sign across $Q_c$. Near extremality the photon-sphere shifts remain finite, whereas the non-degenerate fundamental gravitational-led zero-damping mode is suppressed, $δω/ω\simeq6.0\times10^{3}\,ζ\,(1-Q^2/M^2)$ for $l=2$.

papers.title_en: Landauer bound in a regular Bardeen black hole: extremality and evaporation
papers.abstract_en: Does the vanishing Hawking temperature of an extremal black hole imply that information can be erased without energy transfer? We investigate this question in the regular Bardeen geometry using a two-level quantum system, representing a quantum memory, coupled to a scalar bosonic field confined within an exterior cavity. The Hawking temperature tends to zero at extremality, as does the corresponding thermal Landauer scale. The field in an exterior cavity behaves differently, provided both walls remain away from the horizon, its lowest excitation energy stays finite. For a maximally mixed memory coupled to a reservoir initially in its unique ground state, we find $Q_\infty\geqΔ_{R,\infty}(1/2-ε)$, with $Δ_{R,\infty}$ the reservoir gap and $ε$ the reset error. For a resonant single-mode interaction, we give a reset protocol that attains the bound with no work supplied by the external control. In this example, the memory itself supplies the energy gained by the field. In the multimode calculation, counter-rotating terms are retained. Keeping the pulse parameters unchanged, we find a larger residual reset error closer to extremality. For reservoirs prepared thermally, we evaluate the Reeb--Wolf balance and find that the relative-entropy contribution, expressed in energy units, can have a finite low-temperature limit. These numerical preparations are externally imposed and remain hotter than the Hawking temperature. For comparison, an unconfined scalar field has near-extremal luminosity $P_\infty\propto y^4$, with $y=r_H/|g|-\sqrt2$. Assuming a particular quasistatic energy-loss prescription gives $y\propto t^{-1/2}$; this does not establish the existence of a stable remnant. For this particular reset operation, vanishing Hawking temperature therefore does not force the transferred heat to vanish.

papers.title_en: Identifiability of $g$ mode Resonances in Eccentric Binary Neutron Stars with Multidetector Observations
papers.abstract_en: $g$ mode resonances in eccentric binary neutron star systems are potential probes of internal stratification, superfluidity, composition gradients, and the equation of state. Although such weak dynamical tidal signatures are unlikely to be resolved with current detector sensitivities, third generation observations may make them accessible, in which case identifying the weak resonant phase shift would provide information beyond the bulk adiabatic tidal deformability. We build a four class dataset in an eccentric harmonic framework, containing point particle, adiabatic tide, resonant $g$ mode, and pure noise samples, and use Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) detector data to test whether this weak resonant phase signature can be identified from noisy time domain strain. The ET, CE, and ET+CE deep learning models reach accuracies of $0.650$, $0.809$, and $0.875$, respectively. On the same simulated samples, the matched filtering method reaches lower accuracies of $0.534$, $0.703$, and $0.718$. This result arises from the fact that the resonant correction manifests as a weak phase morphology difference superimposed on the adiabatic tidal background, whereas matched filtering is sensitive only to the overall similarity. Hence, in the presence of weak phase differences, the neural network employed for the classification task is better able to learn these local phase and morphology features from the complete time domain strain segment. The results indicate that joint third generation observations improve the identifiability of weak internal mode phase information.

papers.title_en: AdS${}_3$/BCFT${}_2$ correspondence and 't Hooft anomaly of U(1) symmetry
papers.abstract_en: We investigate how a U(1) 't Hooft anomaly obstructs symmetry-preserving boundary conditions from the perspective of the AdS${}_3$/BCFT${}_2$ correspondence. By considering a U(1) Maxwell--Chern--Simons system in the bulk spacetime, we show that the BCFT current is not conserved at the boundary. We also derive the general solution for the gauge field in AdS${}_2$ slicing.

papers.title_en: The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
papers.abstract_en: We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model with gauge and Higgs fields regulated on a finite bosonic lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This retains the familiar continuum treatment of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes. Standard Model anomaly cancellation permits a consistent, gauge-invariant phase for the massless chiral determinant. Yukawa interactions are incorporated with a gauge-covariant spectral cutoff acting on the interaction vertices, not on the fermion propagator. Under the stated analytic conditions, the cutoff can be removed by the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, yielding a finite, exactly gauge-invariant functional integral at fixed bosonic lattice spacing and spacetime volume, including topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At zero Yukawa coupling and on smooth weak-field backgrounds, we establish agreement between the appropriately chirality-matched overlap and continuum Weyl fermion determinants up to local counterterms. We also establish reflection positivity at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta for a modified gauge-field reconstruction; its continuum equivalence with Craig's original reconstruction is not proved. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.

papers.title_en: PIFFLE: Characterizing Foreground Dispersion Measure Contributions Across 4 Decades in Halo Mass in the FRB20230907D Field
papers.abstract_en: We characterize the foreground environment of FRB20230907D, localized to a galaxy at $z=0.464$, which has an observed dispersion measure of ${\rm DM}_{\rm obs}=1031~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$. At its redshift, FRB20230907D lies above the Macquart relation, the expected relation between cosmological dispersion measure and the source redshift, indicating a substantial excess DM along this line of sight. We use Subaru/PFS and SDSS spectroscopy, published group catalogs, Rubin/LSST imaging, and eROSITA X-ray data to characterize the foreground structures that may account for this excess. A friends-of-friends search identifies a massive foreground system at $z\simeq0.09$ with $M_{\rm vir}\simeq7.7\times10^{14}~M_\odot$, while low redshift catalogs reveal an additional group at $z\simeq0.02565$. Assuming that the halo gas follows a modified-NFW halo density profile, we estimate observer frame contributions of $205^{+30}_{-25}~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$ and $80^{+60}_{-40}~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$ from these systems, respectively. After accounting for the remaining foreground and host contributions, we are able to make the first-ever constraints on the dispersion measure of a closely-intersected $M_*\approx 10^8\,M_\odot$ dwarf galaxy: ${\rm DM}_{\rm UGC7596}=58^{+53}_{-40}~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$ at $b_\perp \approx 0.03\,R_{\rm vir}$, which is consistent with hydrodynamical predictions for low mass halos. This highlights the enhancement of dense foreground spectroscopy and multi-wavelength data toward the interpretation of FRB dispersion measures.

papers.title_en: Primordial tensor mode from the neutrino sector
papers.abstract_en: We show that a regular solution for primordial tensor fluctuations can arise from the higher-order multipoles of the collisionless neutrino distribution after neutrino decoupling. Focusing on the leading case with the neutrino octupole mode (tensor-octupole mode), we derive the initial conditions for the Einstein-Boltzmann system and calculate angular power spectra for the cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies. Compared with the standard gravitational-wave mode, the tensor-octupole mode has a weaker large-scale metric response. It therefore gives a suppressed reionization bump and a different oscillation phase in the tensor CMB power spectra, providing a way to separate it from the standard tensor mode.

papers.title_en: Global Magnetohydrodynamic Simulations of Monster Shocks in Neutron Star Magnetospheres
papers.abstract_en: Waves launched from the neutron star surface or inner magnetosphere propagate through the magnetosphere as small perturbations, but can grow relative to the background magnetic field and steepen into ``monster shocks'' -- ultra-relativistic magnetized shocks which can power high-energy emission. Such shocks can develop around isolated magnetars, merging binaries, and collapsing neutron stars. They occur in magnetically dominated plasma and are described by relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). We present global relativistic MHD simulations of monster shocks in unperturbed and perturbed (``wrinkled'') backgrounds with a global dipolar geometry. Our simulations confirm analytical predictions for equatorial shocks and provide new insight into the behavior of oblique shocks off the equator. Simulations where the shock is formed through Alfvén mode to fast mode conversion are also presented, demonstrating the generic nature of the monster shock mechanism. We explore how the presence of additional modes in the magnetosphere modifies the shock behavior. Modes of comparable amplitude can fragment the shock front, substantially reduce the magnetization, produce localized enhancements in the Lorentz factor relative to an unperturbed dipole background, and intermittently generate additional shocks along a line of sight.

papers.title_en: Modeling of the X-ray Flux and Polarization Energy Spectra of Black Hole X-Ray Binaries with the KerrC Code
papers.abstract_en: In this chapter, we introduce the kerrC model, an advanced framework designed for the analysis of combined spectral and polarimetric X-ray emission from black hole systems. The model is built upon an extensive dataset of ray-tracing Monte Carlo simulations that compute the radiative transfer of X-rays in the strongly curved spacetime near the event horizon of a Kerr black hole. These simulations incorporate thermal seed emission from a geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk, along with the subsequent Comptonization processes within a hot corona of variable geometry and physical properties. Crucially, the reflection of both primary disk and Comptonized photons is treated self-consistently utilizing the xillver reflection tables, and the polarization 4-vectors of the photons are rigorously transported throughout the simulation to preserve full polarization information. The code tracks photons forward in time, allowing for multiple photon scatterings in the corona and off the accretion disk. We detail the underlying mechanics of the ray-tracing simulations and the fitting models, and discuss the applications of kerrC in leveraging X-ray polarization observations to constrain black hole spin and coronal geometry.

papers.title_en: A pipeline for identifying astrophysical signals and instrumental glitches in LISA data
papers.abstract_en: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a space-based gravitational wave detector scheduled for launch in the 2030s by the European Space Agency. Operating in the 0.1 mHz to 0.1 Hz band, LISA will observe a variety of astrophysical sources including but not limited to supermassive black hole mergers, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and white dwarf binaries. LISA will yield new insights, including supermassive black hole formation, new tests of general relativity, population studies of white dwarfs and others. Like all interferometric gravitational wave detectors, LISA data is expected to contain non-astrophysical transients, commonly referred to as glitches. We introduce a two step pipeline that consists of a search algorithm for detecting potential transients in simulated LISA data followed by a machine learning model that classifies the detected transients as gravitational waves or instrumental glitches. This is important for MBHBs with very high masses (around $10^6\ M_{\odot}$) which are transients that could be morphologically similar to LISA glitches in the data. Initial results demonstrate a promising ability to classify detected events with an accuracy close to $98\%$. The pipeline also shows the ability to analyze a month of data in under 2 minutes on a laptop. This shows an eventual utility of our pipeline for enabling accurate rapid alerts from low latency searches. It could also support model selection in global-fit analyses by providing an initial summary of the location and type of individual signals. This paper also discusses challenges encountered during training, including limitations of the current framework.

papers.title_en: Simplicity of the three-point stress-tensor form factor beyond the planar limit
papers.abstract_en: We express the complete three-loop subleading-color finite remainder of the three-point stress-tensor-multiplet form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory as a permutation sum of a single $A_2$-type function. The non-product part of the seed is a combination of 35 weight-six generalized polylogarithms, while all lower-weight products and zeta-value terms belong to the same five-letter algebra. A bootstrap based on independently computed collinear data, branch-cut constraints and empirical final-entry relations determines both the symbol and the full function. The remaining function-level ambiguity is proportional to $ζ_2$ times the two-loop planar remainder and is fixed by a single final-entry relation. The weight-three left coproduct factors of the planar and subleading-color results span the same space modulo products; at weight four, the subleading-color result contains four additional nonclassical directions. Through the established maximal-transcendentality correspondence, this compact representation also describes the weight-six subleading-color sector of Higgs-plus-three-gluon amplitudes in QCD. We also construct a four-loop candidate symbol space under a conjectural extension of the three-loop constraints.

papers.title_en: Quantum Correlations of Neutrinos in the Kerr-Newman Space-time
papers.abstract_en: Quantum phases establish a connection between gravitation and quantum information, offering a novel avenue for exploring the properties of space-time. In this paper, we investigate the quantum correlations (QCs) of neutrinos in the Kerr--Newman space-time for both zero- and nonzero-angular-momentum propagation. The results show that, for zero-angular-momentum propagation, the oscillation periods of the survival probability and QCs progressively decrease with propagation distance in the inward direction. In the outward direction, increasing $M$ lengthens the oscillation periods of $P_{ν_e\rightarrowν_e}$, entanglement, and the monogamy of nonlocality, whereas increasing the angular momentum $a$ or charge $Q$ shortens them. For nonzero-angular-momentum propagation, the metric parameters also generate local profile modulations through additional two-path interference terms, rather than merely rescaling the oscillation period. Furthermore, we find that, despite differences in their ranges of variation, entanglement and coherence exhibit highly consistent oscillatory behavior in both propagation cases. These findings provide a comprehensive understanding of neutrino-based relativistic quantum information.

papers.title_en: The Extended Ultrahigh-energy Gamma-Ray Emission in the Vicinity of PSR J2238+5903
papers.abstract_en: We present a comprehensive analysis of the recently discovered TeV gamma-ray source, LHAASO J2238+5900. Based on data collected from the LHAASO, our fitting results suggest that the source is significantly extended with an angular extension of 0.54° \pm 0.01° and is spatially coincident with the pulsar PSR J2238+5903. Its spectrum is characterized by a power-law with a cutoff at 41.0\pm 3.5 TeV. Additionally, the source exhibits a significant signal of 7.9σabove 100 TeV, implying that it is a PeVatron candidate. While the gamma-ray emission is consistent with a pulsar wind nebula (PWN) scenario, the relatively large extension size also allows for a halo interpretation, potentially caused by electron-positron pairs escaping from the PWN.

papers.title_en: Oppenheimer-Snyder Collapse in Metric f(R) Gravity: Constraints from Generalized Vaidya Exteriors
papers.abstract_en: We study the Oppenheimer--Snyder (OS) collapse problem in metric $f(R)$ gravity by matching a homogeneous dust Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) interior to a generalized Vaidya exterior across a timelike hypersurface. In metric $f(R)$ gravity, regular matching requires the continuity not only of the induced metric and extrinsic curvature, but also of the Ricci scalar and its normal derivative. {For the homogeneous dust interiors considered here, these additional conditions generically exclude Ricci-flat exteriors, such as the Schwarzschild solution.} We show that, for an unrestricted generalized Vaidya exterior, the matching conditions fix the boundary data but do not uniquely determine the bulk extension, leaving open the possibility of a physical resolution of the collapse problem. However, once the exterior matter content is restricted to the generalized Vaidya form, the field equations impose a strong constraint, forcing $f_{,R}$ to be linear in the areal radius, $f_{,R}=A(v)\,r+B(v)$. For locally invertible $f_{,R}$ with $f_{,RR}\neq 0$, this sharply reduces the admissible class of exteriors, so that the matching data uniquely determine the exterior solution on each interval where the boundary map is locally invertible. For branches with $f_{,R}>0$, $f_{,RR}\ne0$, and $f_{,R}$ regular and finite at finite curvature, a globally extended exterior with finite asymptotic curvature requires $A(v)=0$. The matching conditions then force constant curvature. Imposing the null energy condition on both sides leaves only the vacuum-energy component and a locally maximally symmetric geometry. Under these assumptions, nontrivial collapse of spatially flat FLRW perfect-fluid interiors is therefore excluded within the restricted exterior class.

papers.title_en: Asymmetric Dark Matter from Low-Scale Spontaneous Leptogenesis
papers.abstract_en: We investigate a novel type of asymmetric dark matter (ADM) model in which the dark matter asymmetry and the baryon asymmetry in our universe (BAU) are produced simultaneously via low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis, where the mass scale of right-handed neutrino is much lower than the Davidson-Ibarra bound $M_1 \ll 10^{9}~\rm{GeV}$. In our scenario, both asymmetries are predominantly sourced by a dynamical $CP$ phase, namely the majoron. Its kinetic misalignment provides a sufficiently large, time-dependent effective $CP$ phase, allowing efficient asymmetry production even for low-scale right-handed neutrinos. In our framework, the sources of $CP$ violation responsible for the BAU and ADM are correlated with each other, leading to a predictive relation for the dark matter mass. In particular, when the dark matter asymmetry reaches its equilibrium value before freeze-out, the dark matter mass is typically predicted to lie in the range $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_χ \lesssim \mathcal{O}(100)~\mathrm{GeV}$, which lies within the sensitivity of direct detection experiments. On the other hand, if the dark matter asymmetry does not reach its equilibrium value due to weak coupling, the allowed mass range extends over a broader interval, $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_χ \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10)~\rm{TeV}$.

papers.title_en: Residual Galactic binary foreground in LISA stochastic gravitational-wave background inference: source power concentration and spectral degeneracy
papers.abstract_en: Galactic compact binaries are expected to form a dominant millihertz foreground for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), and residual foreground power can bias stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) inference or increase its uncertainty. Using the LISA Data Challenge 2A (LDC2A) injections and the Erebor injection-recovery match, we construct a catalog residual spectrum from 0.4 to 6.0 mHz. We distinguish two effects. The first is the departure from Gaussianity of a sum of source signals with independent random phases, quantified by its excess kurtosis; the second is the spectral degeneracy between the residual and the SGWB in the mean binned power. Source discreteness determines the excess kurtosis of this sum, but instrumental noise and fiducial SGWB power strongly reduce its magnitude in most bins. We quantify this degeneracy with a local Fisher information matrix for the SGWB amplitude $Ω_0$ and the residual-power factor $β$. For a frequency-independent SGWB with $Ω_0=10^{-11}$ and residual power distributed uniformly over the Fourier frequencies within each bin, marginalizing over $β$ increases the $Ω_0$ uncertainty by $13.6\%$ with the Gaussian Fourier-amplitude covariance and by $13.8\%$ with the finite-source diagonal random-phase covariance. Under the Gaussian Fourier-amplitude covariance, the largest allowed prior standard deviation on $β$ that limits this increase to $10\%$ is $0.0073$. With this covariance recomputed at each fiducial amplitude, the uncertainty increase ranges from $12.7\%$ to $20.7\%$ over $10^{-13}\leqΩ_0\leq10^{-10}$. The residual-SGWB spectral degeneracy persists under alternative distributions of residual power over Fourier frequencies and diagonal covariances, while omitting the residual induces a systematic bias in the fitted SGWB amplitude.

papers.title_en: Unlocking Pandora's Secrets: Probing the Thermodynamics of Abell 2744
papers.abstract_en: Abell 2744 (Pandora's Cluster) is a massive galaxy cluster undergoing multiple mergers, characterized by a highly disturbed X-ray morphology, elevated intracluster medium (ICM) temperatures, and several radio relics associated with merger driven shocks. We present NuSTAR observations of Abell 2744 aimed at mapping its thermodynamic structure and constraining the presence of inverse Compton (IC) scattering from relativistic electrons. We measure the temperature distribution across the cluster and identify a prominent shock front with a Mach number of $\mathcal{M} = 1.58^{+0.42}_{-0.30}$, aligning with the southeastern boundary of the radio halo. The global NuSTAR spectra are modeled with single- and two-temperature thermal components, as well as thermal plus power-law models to test for IC emission. The spectra are well described by purely thermal models with an average temperature of $kT \approx 11$ keV, and we find no significant evidence for non-thermal hard X-ray emission. We derive a 90\% confidence upper limit on the $20-80$ keV IC flux of $ F_{\rm nt} < 2.31 \times 10^{-12} erg~s^{-1}~cm^{-2}$. Combining this with 1.5 GHz diffuse radio measurements from the VLA, we estimate a lower limit on the average magnetic field strength of $B > 0.2 \ \rm{μG}$.

papers.title_en: Type IIB Forms and Scalars from an $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
papers.abstract_en: We formulate the scalar and form-field sector of type IIB supergravity as an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary. Unlike the pseudo-action, it is a genuine action principle with manifest global $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ symmetry. The IIB fields arise as edge modes: a boundary term breaks the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, so the axion-dilaton parametrizes $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(2)$, and the boundary field equations give the duality relations, including $F_5$ self-duality. As the action never refers to the axion-dilaton directly, S-duality monodromies become holonomies of a flat connection.

papers.title_en: Gauge-Invariant Fermion
papers.abstract_en: We show that in quantum electrodynamics the Green's functions of the Dirac-dressed fermion coincide, for any value of the gauge parameter in the $R_ξ$ gauge and to all orders in perturbation theory, with those of the undressed fermion in the Landau gauge. The dressed fermion couples only to the transverse photon, and the gauge parameter is confined to a decoupled sector. The dressed vertex then obeys a homogeneous Ward identity, and the dressed field is renormalized multiplicatively with no new counterterm. A partially dressed family realizes the Landau-Khalatnikov-Fradkin relation exactly, and dressings with other kernels reproduce other gauges. Every dressing yields the same pole mass and, with the differences carried by the vertex, the same mass function.

papers.title_en: Optimal Strategies for Gravitational-Wave Memory Detection with Noise Marginalization in Pulsar Timing Arrays
papers.abstract_en: Current pulsar timing arrays could detect gravitational wave memory, which would provide a unique test of general relativity. In order to optimize our searches for gravitational wave memory in pulsar timing arrays, we integrate the optimal frequentist statistics for GW memory into the \texttt{enterprise} code suite. We additionally test a noise marginalized version of this statistic, and compare it's effectiveness to the simpler maximum posterior method. We perform these tests on simulated pulsar timing array with red and white noise content, as well as the NANOGrav $15$-year data set. We find no significant variations in our detection statistics between the noise-marginalized and the maximum-posterior methods for the simulated datasets, and only small variations in the NANOGrav $15$-year comparisons. We conclude that for realistic PTAs the noise-marginalization method could be useful for assigning a false alarm probability to Bayesian results, though the maximum posterior method is sufficient for identifying potentially detectable signals.

papers.title_en: Learning State Preparation Circuits for Quantum Phases of Matter
papers.abstract_en: Many-body ground state preparation is an important subroutine used in the simulation of physical systems. In this paper, we introduce a flexible and efficient framework for obtaining a state preparation circuit for a large class of many-body ground states. We introduce polynomial-time classical algorithms that take reduced density matrices over $\mathcal{O}(1)$-sized balls as inputs, and output a circuit that prepares the global state. We introduce algorithms applicable to (i) short-range entangled states (e.g., states prepared by shallow quantum circuits in any number of dimensions, and more generally, invertible states) and (ii) long-range entangled ground states (e.g., the toric code on a disk). Both algorithms can provably find a circuit whose depth is asymptotically optimal. Our approach uses a variant of the quantum Markov chain condition that remains robust against constant-depth circuits. The robustness of this condition makes our method applicable to a large class of states, whilst ensuring a classically tractable optimization landscape.

papers.title_en: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
papers.abstract_en: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.

papers.title_en: Extragalactic photon-ALP conversion at CTA energies
papers.abstract_en: Magnetic fields in extragalactic space between galaxy clusters may induce conversions between photons and axion-like particles (ALPs), thereby shielding the photons from absorption on the extragalactic background light. For TeV gamma rays, the oscillation length ($l_{\rm osc}$) of the photon-ALP system becomes inevitably of the same order as the coherence length of the magnetic field ($l$) and the length over which the field changes significantly (transition length $l_{\rm t}$) due to refraction on background photons. We derive exact statistical evolution equations for the mean and variance of the photon and ALP transfer functions in the non-adiabatic regime ($l_{\rm osc} \sim l \gg l_{\rm t}$). We also make analytical predictions for the transfer functions in the quasi-adiabatic regime ($l_{\rm osc} \ll l, l_{\rm t}$). Our results are important in light of the upcoming Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA), and may also be applied to models with non-zero ALP masses.

papers.title_en: How Significant are Cosmological Collider Signals in the Planck Data?
papers.abstract_en: The search for primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) is theoretically well motivated but remains observationally challenging. Tight constraints with low significance for the standard non-Gaussian shapes suggest that detection may lie beyond the reach of near-future experiments. However, tests of PNG are highly template-dependent. From a theory perspective, a whole new family of bispectrum shapes arise in the cosmological collider program, with distinct signatures of heavy particles during inflation. In this work, we provide a class of simplified collider templates for these particles that encompasses a broader range of masses, sound speeds, and interactions. We propose that, given the current state of observations, the most effective strategy to search for PNG signals is through orthogonalizing the collider templates, such that they are uncorrelated with the tightly constrained single field predictions. Our results show that removing the single-field contribution enhances the signal across all four templates studied. Using the {\it Modal} pipeline and \textit{Planck} CMB data, we perform a systematic parameter scan of the (\textit{orthogonalized}) collider templates with the most significant result reaching $2.4σ$ for spin-0, after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect; indicative results for spin-1 and spin-2 peak around 2$σ$. These results indicate that, with refined collider templates and improved data analysis strategies, there are credible prospects with forthcoming observations to detect PNG {\it and also} identify the presence of massive particles during inflation.

papers.title_en: Bicoherence States from QPO-Accretion Flow Coupling in Black Hole X-ray Binaries
papers.abstract_en: We calculate the bispectrum of a black hole X-ray binary light curve model where lognormal fluctuations associated with the inner flow are multiplicatively modulated by a quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) and its harmonic. The bispectrum is a third-order Fourier statistic which measures the strength of nonlinear relationships between frequencies in a timeseries. When applied to black hole X-ray binaries, the bispectrum reveals nonlinear coupling between QPOs and the broadband noise. These couplings are sorted into a small set of states and X-ray binaries are observed to transition between these states as they undergo spectral transitions. We show that the model we consider is able to reproduce all of the canonical bispectral states analytically. We consider other sources of incoherent variability which dilute this model light curve and find that changes in this dilution, together with changes in the QPO amplitude, drive the transitions between the bispectral states. We also show that the larger QPO amplitudes of high-inclination sources favor the cross state and the weaker QPOs of low-inclination sources favor the hypotenuse state, which can explain the empirically observed correlation. Additionally, any dilution by equatorial winds, which are seen mainly at high inclination, would push high-inclination sources further toward the cross state.

papers.title_en: Teukolsky equations in perturbations of Kerr
papers.abstract_en: The Kerr stability conjecture has been proved in the slowly rotating case, i.e., $|a|\ll m$, in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen, and extended in \cite{Sze}, by the author, to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The proof in \cite{Sze} crucially relies on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the scalar wave equation and for Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. In addition, two results in \cite{Sze}, concerning the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr and energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky in the setting of \cite{Sze}, are stated without proofs. The goal of the present paper companion paper to \cite{Sze} is to provide the proof of these two results.

papers.title_en: Universal Dark-matter Density Profiles of Cosmic Filaments
papers.abstract_en: We present a comprehensive analysis of the radial dark-matter (DM) density profiles of cosmic filaments in the hydrodynamical simulation TNG50. The cosmic web is extracted from high-resolution density grids at redshifts $z =$ 0, 0.5, 1, 2 and 3 using the DisPerSE algorithm. We show that the filament spine locations returned directly by DisPerSE do not accurately reflect the true density ridges. To address this issue, we introduce a "shrinking-cylinder" re-centering algorithm, which significantly increases the inferred central densities and restores the inner power-law behavior of the profiles. When the radial coordinate is scaled by the virial radii of the terminal nodes, the filament density profiles exhibit a nearly universal form that depends only weakly on redshift, node mass, and filament length. This result suggests that cosmic filaments, much like dark-matter halos, obey a form of structural self-similarity once an appropriate characteristic scale is introduced. By repeating the measurement using only smoothly distributed, unbound DM particles, we find that the apparent central cusp of the full profile is primarily produced by low-mass halos embedded along the filament spines, while the smooth component develops a flat core within $R/R_{\rm vir}\lesssim0.1$. The redshift evolution of this smooth component further suggests a transition from predominantly smooth filamentary accretion at high redshift to increasingly clumpy accretion at late times. Finally, we show that the universal filament profile is accurately described by a generalized triple-power-law model.

papers.title_en: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
papers.abstract_en: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.

papers.title_en: Galaxy and Halo Root Systems: Fingerprints of Mass Assembly
papers.abstract_en: We discuss what we call halo or galaxy root systems, collections of particle pathlines that show the infall of matter from the initial uniform distribution into a collapsed structure. The matter clumps as it falls in; projected through time, it produces filamentary density enhancements analogous to tree roots and branches, or branching river networks. This relates to the larger-scale cosmic web, but is defined locally about one of its nodes: a physical, geometric version of a merger tree. We find dark-matter-halo root systems on average to exhibit more roots and root branches for the largest cluster haloes than for small haloes, indicating their more complicated assembly, even in dark matter without gas physics. Also, we find that high spin manifests as curvier roots, and that many have mass contributions that start far away from central, compact protohalo cores. Root systems also show sensitivity to anisotropic infall, which we see some evidence for in a simulation with rather low box size.

papers.title_en: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
papers.abstract_en: Neutrino-antineutrino annihilation above black-hole accretion discs is shaped both by general-relativistic transport and by neutrino flavour conversion. Whether these effects can be treated independently depends on how gravity weights the different flavour populations. We investigate this interplay using backward ray tracing in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, combined with an exact angular-moment formulation of the annihilation kernel that we validate against the analytic spherical solution and published disc calculations. We first establish that flavour-conversion corrections are independent of the spacetime geometry when conversion is uniform and the initial heavy-lepton neutrino emission is negligible. For uniform conversion, this separability remains approximately valid when the flavour-dependent emitting regions overlap: compared with the same discs in flat space, moving with the same local velocities, gravity enhances the deposited energy by factors of 1.4-5, while changing the relative conversion effect by no more than 6% for most temperature profiles considered; conversion that varies across the disc raises this to 22% around a rapidly spinning hole. A qualitatively different regime emerges when heavy-lepton neutrinos originate from an inner ring separated from the electron-flavour emitting regions. Relativistic bending and energy shifts preferentially enhance annihilations involving inner-ring neutrinos, producing relativistic conversion factors up to 2.4 times the flat-space ones. In one configuration, flavour equipartition reduces the deposition by 54% in flat space but increases it by 11% in Kerr spacetime. These results identify the spatial arrangement of flavour-dependent neutrinospheres as a key determinant, in the models considered, of whether flavour conversion and relativistic transport can be treated separately.

papers.title_en: Late Epoch Infrared Spectroscopy and Two-Component 3D Photoionization Modeling of Classical Nova V5668 Sgr
papers.abstract_en: V5668 Sgr is an Fe II classical nova (CN) that exploded on 15 March 2015. We present near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy of the ejecta from the Mt. Abu observatory which exhibits emission lines of species H, He, N, S, Ti, and Si. We also present SOFIA (+FORCAST) spectroscopy which shows two forbidden emission lines, [Ne II] at 12.8 $μ$m and [O IV] at 25.9 $μ$m, as well as two emission features attributed to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) at 6.2 $μ$m and 11.3 $μ$m. 1D Cloudy photoionization simulations require two components to model the system, which suggests a multifaceted, morphologically complex ejecta. The 1D simulations also reveal He, N, Ne, S, Ti, Si, and O chemical abundances elevated above fiducial solar levels. 3D pyCloudy photoionization emission profiles visualize the ejecta and elucidate the system's complex composition.

papers.title_en: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
papers.abstract_en: First proposed by Milgrom in 1983 as an alternative to the standard Cold Dark Matter (CDM) paradigm, Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) has gained renewed momentum in light of persistent non-detections of exotic dark matter particles and growing tensions facing CDM on galactic scales. While MOND perfectly reproduces galactic rotation curves, it encounters notable challenges in explaining the equilibrium of galaxy clusters. Although it reduces the overall dark matter budget in these massive systems, an unidentified mass component remains required. This paper investigates the hypothesis that this missing mass is baryonic: composed of non-radiating ordinary matter such as stellar remnants, gas too diffuse to initiate star formation, or compact, ultra-dense clouds of cold molecular gas with low volume filling factors. Using a sample of 106 clusters mapped in X-rays, emitted by the hot intra-cluster medium (ICM) composing most of the visible mass, we derive first the total mass within the Newtonian dynamics, assuming hydrostatic equilibrium and spherical symmetry. Then, with the modified Poisson equation, we reconstruct the spatial distribution of the invisible missing matter within the MOND framework. In the sample, the relaxed systems harboring cooling flows, known as cool-core clusters, have the highest peaks of dark missing mass. Its density profile reveals a pronounced central concentration bounded by a steep truncation immediately beyond a core radius of 20-30 kpc, confirming previous studies. MOND reduces the necessary dynamical mass by a factor of 4 to 10. The residual missing mass is proportional to the total gas mass, being roughly twice lower.

papers.title_en: Thirty years of 2D MIT
papers.abstract_en: The zero-magnetic-field metal-insulator transition in strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems was experimentally discovered three decades ago, thereby triggering extensive experimental and theoretical investigations. Prior to this discovery, the occurrence of such a transition --- as well as the very existence of a metallic phase in two dimensions --- was regarded as forbidden within the framework of the one-parameter scaling theory of localization. In this work, we provide a comprehensive review of the transport and thermodynamic properties of two-dimensional electron and hole systems in which carrier-carrier interactions constitute the dominant energy scale. We present and critically analyze both experimental observations and theoretical developments accumulated over the past thirty years.

papers.title_en: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
papers.abstract_en: We present a Wilsonian framework, globally controlled across the holonomy space, for determining the perturbative data governing the vacua of chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on a circle. This allows lifting the Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua in 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ Chern--Simons-matter theories to $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$. The framework is showcased by finding a rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple U(1) model and by reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction (first diagnosed on $S^3\times S^1$) of an SU(2) Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory.

papers.title_en: Alcock-Paczynski Blinding Scheme for the Ly-$α$ Forest Analysis
papers.abstract_en: We present and validate a blinding method for the Lyman-$α$ (Ly$α$) forest analysis based on a modification of the Alcock-Paczynski test. In order to hide the background expansion history, the method employs a geometrical shift of each quasar (QSO) forest in wavelength space, once the quasar continuum has been fitted and the fluctuation field is extracted. The redshift positions for the QSO sample are also changed in a consistent manner. We show that the method remains effective when applied to real data, where contamination from metals and Lyman-$β$ is intrinsically mixed with the Lyman-$α$ forest. This limitation is primarily visible in the 1D correlation function, where other blinding strategies can mitigate the effect. To assess its effectiveness, the prescription is tested against a series of datasets of increasing complexity: from idealized low-noise mocks, to realistic DESI year one synthetic datasets, and finally to data from DESI first data release (DR1), using both the auto (Ly$α\times$Ly$α$) and cross (Ly$α\times$ QSO) correlations. We find that the method robustly shifts the BAO peak position from the 3D correlation functions to the expected value for cosmology changes of around 5\% in the matter content, without altering the shape of the posteriors in the model parameters. In conclusion, this catalog-level blinding strategy is a viable method for cosmological inference with the Lyman-$α$ forest, particularly if a cross-analysis with other tracers using the same blinding strategy is pursued.

papers.title_en: Disentangling Multiple Scaling Dimensions via Operator Covariance in Critical Quantum Spin Systems
papers.abstract_en: We present a general proof of different power-law decays versus distance of the eigenvalues of two-point covariance matrices in critical lattice quantum models, allowing extraction of multiple scaling dimensions. We demonstrate the practical utility of this method in the context of a spin-1/2 chain with critical ground state described by the SU(2)_1 Wess--Zumino--Witten field theory. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute covariance matrices in different symmetry sectors, we resolve the expected relevant and marginal primary operators as well as some descendants. The covariance method can be integrated into many existing numerical schemes and promises to significantly enhance computational studies of quantum criticality.

papers.title_en: Testing influence of tides on gravitational wave emission with SPH code PHANTOM
papers.abstract_en: In this article, we demonstrate how a Newtonian SPH (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics) code PHANTOM can be used to estimate the tidal contribution to gravitational wave (GW) waveforms. Using a binary neutron star (NS+NS) system with typical masses of 1.5 + 1.5 Msun as an example, we show - by comparing our results with waveforms calibrated against full numerical General Relativity (GR) simulations - that the tidal contribution to GWs can be reliably extracted using as few as about 10$^4$ smoothed particles. Naturally, one must account for the difference in neutron star compactness between Newtonian gravity and general relativity. At separations greater than 100 km, the relative tidal contribution falls below the level of numerical noise inherent in SPH; however, at such distances, GW waveforms for point-like sources are sufficient for detection purposes. For a white dwarf-neutron star (WD+NS) binary with typical masses of 0.6 Msun and 1.5 Msun respectively, a much larger number of smoothed particles is required, along with a separation on the order of tens of thousands of kilometers, as tidal mass transfer and the disruption of the white dwarf begin quite rapidly. Nevertheless, these challenges can be overcome, but the approach is not capable of yielding useful results due to the richness of Newtonian effects. In all cases, it is crucial to perform a hydrostatic/hydrodynamic relaxation (HPR) of the initial models; otherwise, the entire GW signal is lost in the numerical noise.

papers.title_en: Nonstandard Dark Matter at Nonlinear Scales
papers.abstract_en: We investigate how two extensions of the standard $Λ$CDM scenario affect the evolution of the matter density and velocity divergence fields, from the linear regime to deeply nonlinear scales, using $N$-body simulations. We consider two well-motivated scenarios in which the canonical properties of dark matter (DM) are modified. In the first scenario, DM interacts with dark energy (DM--DE interaction). In the second scenario, we allow the DM equation-of-state parameter to deviate from the canonical pressureless limit, $w_{\rm DM}=0$. For the coupled DM--DE scenario, we find significant and scale-dependent deviations from $Λ$CDM of order $50$--$100\%$ in the matter power spectrum, persisting throughout the nonlinear regime, with the velocity divergence spectra providing complementary and partially independent sensitivity. For the $w_{\rm DM} \neq 0$ scenario, we find systematic but remarkably small deviations confined within $5\%$ across all scales probed. Our results identify which scales carry the greatest discriminatory power between these nonstandard scenarios and $Λ$CDM. We show that testing these models with current and forthcoming LSS surveys, through the analysis of density and/or velocity fields, will require a deeper theoretical understanding and accurate nonlinear modelling before robust constraints can be derived from observational data.

papers.title_en: Short-term optical monitoring of quadruply imaged quasars
papers.abstract_en: We present two case studies to demonstrate that short-term optical monitoring campaigns of quadruply imaged quasars (quads) reveal their astrophysical potential. Using the Liverpool Telescope and the third facility of the Two-meter Twin Telescope (TTT3), we monitored the quads QSO 2237+0305 and PS J0147+4630 in the gr bands between July 2025 and January 2026. For QSO 2237+0305, the resulting light curves revealed microlensing variability over a timescale of ~150 days. The g-band difference light curve between images A and B was then used to reliably constrain the half-light radius of the g-band source within the 3.5-16 lt-day range (1σ confidence level). For PS J0147+4630, we derived new constraints on the AB and AC time delays from the r-band light curves of the ABC images in an arc-like configuration, obtaining 2σ uncertainties of ~2 days. These constraints were used to shed light on the lensing mass distribution. Overall, our results validate the design of short-term optical monitoring campaigns of quads as valuable astrophysical tools in the era of large-scale surveys. The proof of concept relies on observations with ground-based 2mclass telescopes that lack sophisticated systems to correct for optical distortions caused by atmospheric turbulence, and we indicate the astro-photometric properties of the targets and the monitoring strategies needed to achieve success with these telescopes. Additionally, this work represents the first validation of the TTT3 facility for precision photometric monitoring of gravitationally lensed quasars.

papers.title_en: VENUS: Strong Lens Mass Models and Einstein Radii of 60 Galaxy Clusters
papers.abstract_en: We present the strong lens mass modeling result of 60 galaxy clusters targeted by Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS), the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) multi-epoch Treasury program. We obtain refined mass models for the 60 clusters with the glafic software by fitting positions of $\sim 4500$ multiple images, $\sim 1150$ of which are newly identified multiple images with help of multi-band JWST images. Each cluster contains typically $\sim 50$ multiple images, thanks to the selection of target clusters based on their high lensing strengths. We validate our models with the Jackknife method. The median Einstein radius is $\sim 30''$ and the distribution of the Einstein radii extends out to $\sim 60''$ for the source redshift of 9, which confirms that their lensing strengths are indeed among the highest known to date. For the source redshift of 9, we identify MACS J0717.5+3745, MACS J0600.1$-$2008, and PLCK G287.0+32.9 as clusters with the largest Einstein radii as well as the largest areas of the high-magnification ($|μ|>10$) regions. We find that the observed Einstein radii of VENUS clusters are fully compatible with the standard cold dark matter model.

papers.title_en: Wormhole-induced gravi-axion mass distributions and the second-harmonic crossover
papers.abstract_en: We compute the distribution of the wormhole-induced gravi-axion curvature mass across baby-universe sectors when the first two harmonics are retained.
